key_insight: Laser power, welding speed, and TIG current jointly control molten-pool flow, penetration, and arc stability in laser-TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel.
engineering_relevance: The results provide process guidance for tuning hybrid-welding parameters to improve weld geometry and arc behavior in low-expansion Invar steel components.
method: High-speed photography of arc and pool behavior
Parameter sweep over laser power, welding speed, and welding current
evidence_signal: The abstract reports simulation and imaging evidence across laser power (5–6 kW), speed (0.5–0.8 m/min), and current (150–170 A) showing consistent changes in penetration depth, weld width, flow intensity, and arc deformation/stability.
watch_item: The findings are parameter-range specific, so process windows may need revalidation for different joint geometries, thicknesses, or equipment setups.
paper_title: Molten pool dynamic behavior and arc characteristics in laser-TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel
